question: Explain how retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) works, and summarize its main benefits and limitations.
groundTruth: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant documents from an external knowledge source, usually with a retriever over a vector index of embeddings, and adds them to the prompt so a language model generates an answer grounded in that retrieved context. It was introduced by Lewis et al. in 2020. Benefits: more factual and up-to-date answers without retraining, fewer hallucinations, the ability to cite sources, and use of private or domain-specific data. Limitations: answer quality depends on retrieval quality, irrelevant or conflicting passages can mislead the model, context window limits, added latency and cost, and the model can still hallucinate or ignore the retrieved text.
notes: Scored with token-level F1 against this reference (optionally LLM-as-judge with --judge).
